USER REQUEST:
Write a polynomial-time reduction from Subset Sum to Partition. problems.py defines both problems: SOURCE is Subset Sum and TARGET is Partition. The SOURCE and TARGET class docstrings give the exact instance formats, yes-conditions and edge cases.

PROBLEM DEFINITIONS (the SOURCE and TARGET docstrings from problems.py, complete as given here):

SOURCE = SubsetSum
Subset Sum.

Instance: {"numbers": [a1, a2, ...], "target": t}
  * The numbers are non-negative integers of any size; values may repeat.
  * The target is any integer.

Yes iff some sub-list of the numbers (each position used at most once)
sums to exactly t.

Edge cases: t = 0 is always yes (the empty sub-list). t < 0 is always
no. An empty list is yes only for t = 0.

TARGET = Partition
Partition.

Instance: {"numbers": [a1, a2, ...]}
  * The numbers are non-negative integers of any size; values may repeat.

Yes iff the positions can be split into two groups whose numbers have
equal sums (every position goes in exactly one group).

Edge cases: an empty list is yes (two empty groups). An odd total is
always no. Zeros never change the answer.

INPUT FILES: ["problems.py"]
WORKING DIRECTORY: /tmp/reduction-8ew3t0vn
All input files are in this directory; run every command from it and write your files here. problems.py is long (about 500 lines): you do not need to read it to know the formats, which are given above.     reduce(instance) -> instance

The answer to the returned instance must be yes exactly when the answer to the input instance is yes, and reduce must run in polynomial time. Do not call the brute-force solvers inside reduce.

You may read files such as problems.py, but do not run, execute or test any code. Write reduce.py, then submit.

"""Polynomial-time reduction from Subset Sum to Partition.

Source instance: {"numbers": [a1, a2, ...], "target": t}
Target instance: {"numbers": [a1, a2, ...]}

Let S = sum(numbers).  Add one extra number

    x = abs(S - 2*t)

and return {"numbers": numbers + [x]}.

Why this works
--------------
Write A for the original list and consider P = A + [x].

* If t < 0, then x = S - 2t and the total of P is 2*(S - t), so each
  partition group would need sum S - t.  The group not containing x would
  need a subset of A of sum S - t > S, impossible; the group containing x
  would need a subset of A of sum t < 0, also impossible.  Hence P is no,
  matching Subset Sum.

* If t > S, then x = 2t - S and the total of P is 2t, so each group would
  need sum t.  The group not containing x would need a subset of A of sum
  t > S, impossible; the group containing x would need x plus a subset of A
  to equal t, i.e. a subset of sum S - t < 0, also impossible.  Hence P is
  no, matching Subset Sum.

* If 0 <= t <= S, then x = abs(S - 2t) and the total of P is
  S + |S - 2t|, which is even.  Its half is max(S - t, t).
    - If some subset B of A has sum t, then either B (when t is the larger
      half) or A \ B (when S - t is the larger half) gives one partition
      group, and the rest of P gives the other.
    - Conversely, in any equal partition of P, the group not containing x
      has sum equal to the half; if that half is t we are done, and if it is
      S - t then its complement in A has sum t.
  Thus P is yes exactly when some subset of A sums to t.

The extra number has O(size of the input) bits, so the construction runs in
polynomial time and does not solve either problem.
"""


def reduce(instance):
    """Reduce a Subset Sum instance to a Partition instance."""
    numbers = instance["numbers"]
    target = instance["target"]
    extra = abs(sum(numbers) - 2 * target)
    return {"numbers": list(numbers) + [extra]}

  partition group would need sum S - t.  The group not containing x would
  need a subset of A of sum S - t > S, impossible; the group containing x
  would need a subset of A of sum t < 0, also impossible.  Hence P is no,
  matching Subset Sum.

* If t > S, then x = 2t - S and the total of P is 2t, so each group would
  need sum t.  The group not containing x would need a subset of A of sum
  t > S, impossible; the group containing x would need x plus a subset of A
  to equal t, i.e. a subset of sum S - t < 0, also impossible.  Hence P is
  no, matching Subset Sum.

* If 0 <= t <= S, then x = abs(S - 2t) and the total of P is
  S + |S - 2t|, which is even.  Its half is max(S - t, t).

      half) or A \ B (when S - t is the larger half) gives one partition
      group, and the rest of P gives the other.
    - Conversely, in any equal partition of P, the group not containing x
      has sum equal to the half; if that half is t we are done, and if it is
      S - t then its complement in A has sum t.
  Thus P is yes exactly when some subset of A sums to t.

The extra number has O(size of the input) bits, so the construction runs in
polynomial time and does not solve either problem.

def reduce(instance):
    """Reduce a Subset Sum instance to a Partition instance."""
    numbers = instance["numbers"]
    target = instance["target"]
    extra = abs(sum(numbers) - 2 * target)
    return {"numbers": list(numbers) + [extra]}
